metadata.title: Plant Toxicity and Safety Guide
metadata.purpose: Help the general public understand plant toxicity, exposure risks, symptoms, first aid, and prevention.

toxicity_levels.Critical: Potentially life-threatening poisoning or severe injury may occur. Urgent professional advice may be necessary.
toxicity_levels.High: Serious poisoning or injury is possible under certain exposure conditions.
toxicity_levels.Moderate: Harmful effects are possible depending on the plant part, amount, and exposure route.
toxicity_levels.Low: Risk is generally limited under specified conditions, but some plant parts or preparations may still be harmful.
toxicity_levels.Unknown: The plant identity or available evidence is insufficient to assess its toxicity reliably.

general_safety_rules: Do not assume a plant is safe because it is natural or traditionally used.
Avoid touching plant sap, seeds, or unfamiliar plant material unnecessarily.
Wash hands after handling unfamiliar plants.
Avoid rubbing eyes after handling plants.
Ordinary smelling of an intact plant is different from inhaling concentrated oils, smoke, or dust.
Keep potentially toxic plants and seeds away from children and pets.
Do not induce vomiting after suspected plant poisoning unless a medical professional specifically instructs you to do so.
For suspected poisoning, contact a medical professional or poison information service promptly.
Seek emergency care for breathing difficulty, seizures, fainting, severe confusion, or other serious symptoms.

first_aid_guidance.skin_contact: Remove contaminated clothing if necessary and wash the affected skin with soap and water. Seek medical advice if irritation is severe or persists.
first_aid_guidance.eye_contact: Rinse the eye immediately with clean, gently flowing water for 15 to 20 minutes. Seek urgent medical advice, particularly after contact with irritating sap or concentrated oils.
first_aid_guidance.swallowed_plant: Remove any remaining plant material from the mouth. Do not induce vomiting or use home remedies. Contact a medical professional or poison information service promptly.
first_aid_guidance.inhalation: Move to fresh air if it is safe to do so. Seek urgent medical care if breathing difficulty, persistent coughing, or other serious symptoms occur.
first_aid_guidance.emergency: Contact local emergency medical services immediately for seizures, loss of consciousness, breathing difficulty, collapse, or severe symptoms.

plants.short_warning: Castor seeds contain ricin, a highly toxic protein.
plants.why_it_is_harmful: Ricin can interfere with the body's ability to make proteins and can damage cells and organs.

eating.advice: Never eat castor seeds. Chewed or crushed seeds can cause serious poisoning.

skin_contact.advice: Avoid crushing seeds or handling damaged plant material unnecessarily. Wash hands after contact.

eye_contact.advice: Avoid transferring plant material to the eyes. Rinse immediately if exposure occurs.

smelling.risk: Usually low for an intact plant
smelling.advice: Ordinary smelling is not the usual poisoning route. Avoid inhaling dust produced by crushing or grinding seeds.

possible_symptoms: Severe organ damage in serious cases
what_to_do: Seek urgent medical or poison-control advice if seeds are swallowed.
Do not wait for symptoms to appear.
Do not induce vomiting.
prevention: Keep seeds away from children and pets.
Do not crush or chew the seeds.
Wash hands after handling plant material.
plants.important_note: The risk depends on whether seeds were chewed, the amount swallowed, and other exposure circumstances.

plants.short_warning: The milky sap can irritate skin and eyes, and swallowing plant material can be dangerous.
plants.why_it_is_harmful: Calotropis plants contain irritating latex and biologically active cardiac glycosides that can affect the digestive system and heart.

eating.advice: Do not eat the leaves, flowers, stems, or sap. Seek medical advice promptly after swallowing any part.

skin_contact.advice: Avoid direct contact with milky sap. Wash exposed skin with soap and water.

eye_contact.advice: Sap can cause serious eye irritation or injury. Rinse with clean running water for 15 to 20 minutes and seek urgent medical care.

smelling.advice: Smelling an intact flower is not equivalent to swallowing sap. Avoid inhaling spray or particles from cutting or processing the plant.

possible_symptoms: Potential heart rhythm disturbances after significant ingestion
what_to_do: Wash exposed skin thoroughly.
Rinse eyes immediately after sap exposure and seek urgent medical advice.
Seek prompt medical assessment after swallowing plant material.
Seek emergency care for fainting, breathing difficulty, severe vomiting, or an abnormal heartbeat.
prevention: Avoid contact with milky sap.
Do not rub the eyes after handling the plant.
Keep plant parts away from children and pets.
plants.important_note: Confirm the exact Calotropis species where possible. Toxicity depends on the part and amount involved.

plants.short_warning: The local name may refer to different plants. Confirm the species before assigning a toxicity level.
plants.why_it_is_harmful: If the plant is oleander, it contains cardiac glycosides that can disrupt heart function. The local name alone is not sufficient to confirm this identification.

eating.advice: Do not eat any part until the plant has been reliably identified.

skin_contact.advice: Avoid unnecessary contact with unidentified plant sap. Wash hands after handling.

eye_contact.advice: Avoid eye contact. Rinse immediately if sap or plant material enters the eyes.

smelling.advice: Do not assume toxicity from the local name alone. Avoid inhaling smoke from burning plant material.

what_to_do: Obtain reliable botanical identification.
Do not consume the plant while identification is uncertain.
Seek prompt medical advice after suspected ingestion.
prevention: Photograph the leaves, flowers, and stem for identification.
Do not assign species-specific warnings based only on a regional name.
plants.important_note: If confirmed as Nerium oleander, reassess this record using verified oleander toxicology information.

plants.scientific_name: Cinnamomum camphora or a camphor-containing product
plants.short_warning: Swallowing camphor or concentrated camphor products can cause severe poisoning and seizures.
plants.why_it_is_harmful: Camphor can affect the brain and nervous system, potentially causing agitation, confusion, and seizures.

eating.advice: Never swallow camphor crystals or camphor-containing products. Keep them away from children.

skin_contact.advice: Concentrated products can irritate skin. Follow product safety instructions and wash off accidental exposure.

eye_contact.advice: Avoid contact with camphor oils and products. Rinse the eyes with clean running water for 15 to 20 minutes.

smelling.advice: Avoid prolonged exposure to concentrated vapours, especially in poorly ventilated spaces. Ordinary brief exposure is not the same as swallowing camphor.

what_to_do: Seek urgent medical or poison-control advice after swallowing camphor.
Do not induce vomiting.
Call emergency services if seizures, confusion, or breathing problems occur.
prevention: Store camphor securely.
Do not use camphor products internally unless explicitly approved by a qualified medical professional.
plants.important_note: A plant and a manufactured camphor product are not interchangeable records. Verify the source and product formulation.

plants.short_warning: Concentrated eucalyptus oil can cause serious poisoning if swallowed.
plants.why_it_is_harmful: Concentrated eucalyptus oil contains compounds such as 1,8-cineole that can affect the nervous system and cause seizures.

eating.advice: Never swallow eucalyptus essential oil. Do not consume leaves as a home remedy without qualified advice.

skin_contact.advice: Avoid direct contact with concentrated oil. Wash exposed skin and seek advice if irritation occurs.

eye_contact.advice: Rinse immediately with clean running water for 15 to 20 minutes if oil enters the eyes.

smelling.risk: Usually low for an intact tree; higher with concentrated vapours
smelling.advice: Ordinary smelling of a tree is not equivalent to swallowing essential oil. Avoid strong vapours if they cause irritation or breathing symptoms.

what_to_do: Seek urgent medical advice after swallowing eucalyptus oil.
Do not induce vomiting.
Seek emergency care for seizures, severe drowsiness, or breathing difficulty.
prevention: Keep essential oils away from children.
Do not swallow concentrated oils.
Use products according to their safety instructions.
plants.important_note: The risks from concentrated oil differ substantially from those associated with simply being near an intact eucalyptus tree.

plants.short_warning: This ornamental plant contains potent alkaloids and should not be eaten.
plants.why_it_is_harmful: The plant contains alkaloids that affect cell processes. Related compounds have important medical uses under controlled conditions, but the plant itself is not safe for self-medication.

eating.risk: Moderate; exact risk depends on amount and plant part
eating.advice: Do not eat any part or prepare it as a home remedy. Contact a medical professional if swallowed.

skin_contact.advice: Avoid unnecessary handling and wash hands afterward. Stop contact if irritation occurs.

eye_contact.advice: Rinse with clean running water if plant material enters the eyes.

smelling.advice: Smelling the intact plant is not a usual poisoning route. Avoid inhaling smoke from burning plant material.

possible_symptoms: Other effects depending on the amount consumed
what_to_do: Seek medical advice after ingestion.
Do not use the plant to self-treat disease.
Seek urgent help if severe symptoms occur.
prevention: Do not consume ornamental plants.
Keep plant material away from children and pets.
plants.important_note: The toxicity of an accidental exposure should not be equated directly with the risks of purified medicines derived from related compounds.

plants.short_warning: Lantana can be toxic, and unripe berries should not be eaten.
plants.why_it_is_harmful: Lantana contains triterpenoids that can damage the liver. Serious toxicity is particularly well documented in grazing animals.

eating.advice: Do not eat the berries or other plant parts. Seek advice if swallowed.

skin_contact.advice: Some people develop irritation after contact. Wash hands and exposed skin.

eye_contact.advice: Avoid rubbing the eyes after contact. Rinse with clean running water if exposure occurs.

smelling.advice: The normal smell of the plant is not a typical poisoning route. Avoid inhaling smoke from burning it.

possible_symptoms: Potential liver injury after significant ingestion
what_to_do: Seek medical advice after ingestion.
Seek urgent care for persistent vomiting, jaundice, or severe symptoms.
prevention: Do not eat wild berries.
Keep children and pets away from berries and leaves.
plants.important_note: Human toxicity evidence and risk may differ from the well-established effects in livestock.

plants.short_warning: Confirm the botanical identity before applying rue-specific safety warnings.
plants.why_it_is_harmful: If confirmed as Ruta graveolens, its compounds can cause skin sensitivity to sunlight, and ingestion may cause adverse effects.

eating.advice: Do not consume an unidentified plant or its extracts.

skin_contact.risk: Potentially high for confirmed rue under sunlight
skin_contact.advice: If the plant is confirmed as rue, avoid sap contact and sun exposure on contaminated skin. Wash the area thoroughly.

eye_contact.advice: Rinse immediately if sap enters the eyes and seek medical advice if irritation persists.

smelling.advice: Avoid inhaling concentrated vapours or smoke.

what_to_do: Confirm the botanical species.
Wash exposed skin promptly.
Seek medical advice after ingestion or severe skin reactions.
prevention: Avoid handling unidentified plants unnecessarily.
Do not use concentrated plant extracts as home remedies.
plants.important_note: The scientific name and exposure guidance require confirmation because regional names can refer to different species.

plants.short_warning: Neem oil can cause serious poisoning, especially in children.
plants.why_it_is_harmful: Neem oil contains biologically active compounds that can affect the nervous system and other organs when swallowed.

eating.risk: High for neem oil; other preparations vary
eating.advice: Never swallow neem oil. Seek urgent medical advice after accidental ingestion.

skin_contact.risk: Usually low to moderate, depending on preparation
skin_contact.advice: Avoid contact with concentrated products. Wash exposed skin if irritation occurs.

eye_contact.advice: Rinse immediately with clean running water if oil or plant material enters the eyes.

smelling.advice: Avoid inhaling concentrated sprays or vapours.

what_to_do: Seek urgent medical or poison-control advice after neem oil ingestion.
Do not induce vomiting.
Seek emergency care for seizures, altered consciousness, or breathing difficulty.
prevention: Keep neem oil away from children.
Do not swallow concentrated preparations.
Use topical products only according to their instructions.
plants.important_note: The safety of traditional or topical uses should not be generalized to swallowed neem oil.

plants.toxicity_level: Low to Moderate when improperly prepared
plants.short_warning: Raw or inadequately cooked taro can irritate the mouth and throat.
plants.why_it_is_harmful: Taro contains calcium oxalate crystals that can cause a stinging or burning sensation when raw or insufficiently cooked.
dangerous_parts: Leaves and stems if improperly prepared

eating.risk: Moderate when raw or inadequately cooked
eating.advice: Do not eat taro raw. Prepare it thoroughly using an appropriate cooking method.

skin_contact.advice: Raw plant material may irritate sensitive skin. Wash hands after handling.

eye_contact.advice: Avoid rubbing the eyes after handling raw plant material. Rinse with clean running water if exposed.

smelling.advice: Ordinary smelling is not a typical poisoning route.

possible_symptoms: Burning or stinging in the mouth
Swelling or difficulty swallowing in serious cases
what_to_do: Stop eating if burning or irritation occurs.
Rinse the mouth gently with water.
Seek urgent medical care for throat swelling or difficulty breathing or swallowing.
prevention: Cook taro thoroughly.
Do not eat unidentified wild taro-like plants.
plants.important_note: Properly identified and appropriately cooked taro is a common food. Do not label all prepared taro as poisonous.

plants.toxicity_level: Low for ripe fruit; higher concern for green parts
plants.short_warning: Ripe tomatoes are commonly eaten, but leaves, stems, and certain unripe parts should not be consumed in quantity.
plants.why_it_is_harmful: Tomato plants contain glycoalkaloids, including tomatine, especially in green plant tissues. Large exposures may cause adverse effects.
dangerous_parts: Large amounts of green plant material

eating.advice: Ripe tomatoes are generally safe to eat as food. Avoid eating tomato leaves and stems or large amounts of green plant material.

skin_contact.advice: Ordinary handling is generally safe. Wash hands if irritation occurs.

eye_contact.advice: Rinse the eyes with clean water if plant sap or debris enters them.

smelling.advice: The normal smell of the plant is not a typical poisoning route.

what_to_do: Seek medical advice if a large amount of leaves or green plant material is swallowed.
Seek urgent care for severe or persistent symptoms.
prevention: Eat tomatoes prepared as food.
Do not use tomato leaves as food or herbal medicine.
plants.important_note: Do not describe ordinary consumption of ripe tomatoes as poisonous.

plants.toxicity_level: Unknown; potentially High for raw kidney beans
plants.short_warning: Some beans are dangerous when raw or undercooked.
plants.why_it_is_harmful: Raw or inadequately cooked kidney beans can contain phytohaemagglutinin, a lectin that can cause acute digestive illness.
dangerous_parts: Raw or inadequately cooked beans of susceptible species

eating.risk: Potentially high for raw or undercooked kidney beans
eating.advice: Identify the bean species and follow reliable cooking instructions. Never eat raw kidney beans.

skin_contact.advice: Ordinary handling is generally safe. Wash hands after handling.

eye_contact.advice: Avoid rubbing eyes after handling plant material.

smelling.advice: Ordinary smelling is not a typical poisoning route.

what_to_do: Seek medical advice after eating raw or inadequately cooked kidney beans if symptoms develop or exposure is substantial.
Seek urgent care for severe dehydration or persistent vomiting.
prevention: Identify the bean species.
Cook susceptible beans thoroughly according to trusted food-safety instructions.
plants.important_note: The generic name Beans covers many species with different safety profiles. Do not apply kidney-bean warnings to every bean species.

plants.toxicity_level: Low to Moderate depending on species and preparation
plants.short_warning: Some raw bamboo shoots contain cyanogenic compounds and require proper preparation.
plants.why_it_is_harmful: Certain bamboo shoots contain compounds that can release cyanide if not appropriately processed and cooked.
dangerous_parts: Raw or improperly prepared shoots of susceptible species

eating.advice: Do not eat raw wild bamboo shoots. Use a reliable preparation method suitable for the identified species.

skin_contact.advice: Avoid injury from sharp plant surfaces and wash hands after handling.

eye_contact.advice: Avoid contact with plant debris and rinse the eyes if exposed.

smelling.advice: Ordinary smelling is not a typical poisoning route.

possible_symptoms: Potential serious systemic symptoms in severe cyanide poisoning
what_to_do: Seek urgent medical advice after eating raw or improperly prepared shoots if poisoning is suspected.
Call emergency services for breathing difficulty, collapse, or confusion.
prevention: Identify the bamboo species.
Follow established food-preparation guidance.
Do not assume all bamboo shoots are safe raw.
plants.important_note: Risk varies considerably by species and preparation.

plants.short_warning: Confirm the local plant name and species before assigning a toxicity rating.
plants.why_it_is_harmful: If the intended plant is Annona squamosa, its seeds and some other plant parts contain biologically active compounds. This identification must be verified.

eating.advice: Do not eat unidentified plant parts or seeds. For confirmed custard apple, do not chew or eat the seeds.

skin_contact.advice: Avoid unnecessary contact with unidentified sap or crushed seeds.

eye_contact.advice: Rinse immediately if sap or plant material enters the eyes.

smelling.advice: Do not infer toxicity from smell alone.

what_to_do: Confirm the botanical identity.
Seek medical advice if unidentified seeds or plant material are swallowed.
prevention: Do not chew seeds.
Keep unidentified plant material away from children.
plants.important_note: Do not infer the species or toxicity profile from the regional name alone.

plants.toxicity_level: Low to Moderate; strong irritation is possible
plants.short_warning: Chilli can irritate the skin, eyes, mouth, and respiratory tract.
plants.why_it_is_harmful: Capsaicin activates sensory nerves that produce burning and pain. It is an irritant rather than a typical systemic plant poison at ordinary food exposures.
dangerous_parts: Seeds and internal fruit tissues contaminated with capsaicin

eating.risk: Usually low as food; irritation can be intense
eating.advice: Avoid eating chilli that causes severe discomfort. Seek help for severe or persistent symptoms.

skin_contact.advice: Avoid touching your face after handling chilli. Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water.

eye_contact.advice: Rinse with clean running water for 15 to 20 minutes. Remove contact lenses if easily possible and seek medical advice if pain persists.

smelling.advice: Ordinary smelling of a chilli is not the usual risk. Avoid inhaling chilli powder, cooking fumes, or aerosolized extracts.

what_to_do: Wash exposed skin with soap and water.
Rinse exposed eyes immediately.
Move to fresh air after inhaling irritating dust or fumes.
Seek medical attention for persistent eye pain or breathing difficulty.
prevention: Avoid touching the eyes after handling chilli.
Wash hands and utensils after preparation.
Avoid inhaling chilli powder.
plants.important_note: Ordinary culinary exposure differs from concentrated capsaicin extracts and aerosol exposure.

plants.short_warning: The yellow latex beneath the leaf skin can cause severe diarrhea and dehydration if swallowed.
plants.why_it_is_harmful: Aloe latex contains anthraquinone compounds, including aloin, which have laxative effects and can cause fluid and electrolyte loss.

eating.risk: Moderate to high for latex or unprocessed products
eating.advice: Do not swallow aloe latex or unprocessed whole-leaf preparations. Use only appropriately prepared products intended for consumption.

skin_contact.risk: Usually low, but irritation or allergy is possible
skin_contact.advice: Stop use and wash the skin if redness, itching, or irritation occurs.

eye_contact.advice: Rinse immediately with clean running water if sap or gel causes irritation.

smelling.advice: Ordinary smelling is not a typical poisoning route.

what_to_do: Seek medical advice after swallowing aloe latex or an unprocessed preparation.
Seek urgent help for severe diarrhea, weakness, fainting, or signs of dehydration.
prevention: Do not consume yellow latex.
Do not assume every aloe preparation is suitable for eating.
plants.important_note: Topical gel and oral latex have different risk profiles.

plants.scientific_name: Often Tinospora cordifolia; local identification requires confirmation
plants.short_warning: Some preparations associated with Tinospora cordifolia have been linked to liver injury.
plants.why_it_is_harmful: Liver injury has been reported in some people using Tinospora cordifolia preparations. The precise cause and individual risk can vary.
toxic_compounds: Not conclusively established as a single responsible compound

eating.advice: Do not consume unidentified plant material or concentrated herbal preparations without qualified advice.

skin_contact.advice: Wash hands after handling and stop contact if irritation occurs.

eye_contact.advice: Rinse immediately if sap enters the eyes.

smelling.advice: Ordinary smelling is not a typical route for the reported liver injury.

possible_symptoms: Yellowing of the skin or eyes in cases of liver injury
what_to_do: Stop using a suspected product and contact a medical professional if adverse symptoms develop.
Seek urgent medical evaluation for jaundice, dark urine, or severe abdominal symptoms.
prevention: Verify the plant species.
Avoid unsupervised use of concentrated herbal preparations.
Tell a healthcare professional about herbal products being used.
plants.important_note: The regional name and species should be verified. Do not present every traditional preparation as equally toxic.

plants.toxicity_level: Low for ordinary external use of pure henna; product-dependent
plants.short_warning: Some henna products cause allergic reactions. Black henna may contain dangerous additives.
plants.why_it_is_harmful: Pure henna can cause skin reactions in some people. Products marketed as black henna may contain para-phenylenediamine or other additives that can cause severe allergic reactions.
dangerous_parts: Products containing irritating or allergenic additives

eating.advice: Henna products are not food. Do not swallow them.

skin_contact.risk: Low for many pure products; potentially high for adulterated products
skin_contact.advice: Use products from reliable sources and stop use if itching, redness, swelling, or blistering develops.

eye_contact.advice: Rinse immediately with clean running water if the product enters the eyes.

smelling.advice: Avoid inhaling powder or strong chemical fumes, and use products in a well-ventilated area.

possible_symptoms: Severe allergic reactions in susceptible individuals
what_to_do: Stop using the product if a reaction develops.
Wash the affected area gently.
Seek urgent care for facial swelling, breathing difficulty, or a widespread severe reaction.
prevention: Avoid products with unknown ingredients.
Do not assume black henna is pure henna.
Follow product safety instructions.
plants.important_note: The risks of pure henna and adulterated cosmetic products are different.

plants.toxicity_level: Low for normal food varieties; potentially High for unusually bitter fruit
plants.short_warning: Unusually bitter pumpkin or squash may contain harmful cucurbitacins.
plants.why_it_is_harmful: Some cucurbit plants produce cucurbitacins, bitter compounds that can cause severe gastrointestinal illness.
toxic_compounds: Cucurbitacins in certain varieties or plants

eating.risk: Low for normal food varieties; potentially high for unusually bitter fruit
eating.advice: Do not eat pumpkin or squash that tastes unusually bitter. Discard it rather than trying to make it safe by cooking.

skin_contact.advice: Ordinary handling is generally safe. Wash hands after handling.

eye_contact.advice: Rinse the eyes if plant sap or debris enters them.

smelling.advice: Ordinary smelling is not a typical poisoning route.

what_to_do: Stop eating an unusually bitter fruit immediately.
Seek medical advice if any amount of unusually bitter fruit is swallowed and symptoms occur.
Seek urgent care for severe vomiting or diarrhea.
prevention: Do not eat unusually bitter cucurbit fruits.
Do not rely on cooking to remove cucurbitacins.
plants.important_note: Normal edible pumpkin is not generally considered poisonous. Unusual bitterness is an important warning sign.

plants.why_it_is_harmful: A reliable toxicity explanation cannot be provided until the intended species or product is identified.

skin_contact.advice: Avoid unnecessary contact and wash hands after handling.

eye_contact.advice: Rinse immediately if plant material enters the eyes.

smelling.advice: Do not infer toxicity from smell alone. Avoid inhaling smoke or dust from unidentified plant material.

what_to_do: Obtain a photograph and reliable botanical identification.

eye_contact.advice: Rinse immediately if sap or plant material enters the eyes.
